tasks.short: Direct daily operations, priorities, standards, and deadlines.

steps.what: Direct daily operations, analyzing workflow and deadlines
Assemble open workflow counts from the ticket log
Setting priorities and establishing standards for the department

outputs: filed copy of signed daily priority list v1

tasks.design: A dashboard on {HELPDESK} counts open work. The manager directs the day, sets priorities and standards, signs the list in {DOCS}, and a job publishes that version. The list does not assign a score to a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Priorities were reset in a meeting with no shared count of the queue.
tasks.enabler_now: The ticket log can be counted without a new platform.
tasks.still_hard: A deadline still depends on what the manager knows is urgent.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sets the order of work and the standard for the day.

ambition.what: Publish a priority list the same day the queue count changes, only after signing that version.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the morning on priorities, not on counting tickets.

evidence.claim: The management digest says security and IT work uses ticket and incident-log configuration, and judgement stays manual.
Digest [S10] bars a significant decision about a person made solely by automation, so assignment and hiring stay with the manager.

assumptions: Counts are ticket totals, not a score of a person.
Configure the existing ticket log before a new store.
unknowns: Which queue is the department's official one.
Who else must see the priority list.
research_questions: How often urgent work never becomes a ticket.

already_counted.description: Directing the day stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only assembly and filing move to a job. The meeting, the decision, and the signature stay with the manager, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet peers and vendors to solicit cooperation and resolve problems.

steps.what: Meet department heads, managers, and supervisors
Solicit cooperation and resolve problems with vendors

outputs: filed copy of signed cooperation note v1

tasks.design: The meetings stay with the manager. A job files the cooperation note in {DOCS} only after the manager signs that version. No vendor is answered by a job.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agreement lived in someone's memory after the call.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed note can be filed in the existing document store.
tasks.still_hard: Cooperation still depends on the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what problem is resolved and what is asked of the vendor.
tasks.altitude: Meeting time does not shrink. Filing the signed note does.

reach.task: Act on the signed cooperation note
reach.learn: Which problem the note says is closed

evidence.claim: The management digest says security and IT work uses ticket and incident-log configuration, and judgement stays manual.
The management digest says a records path can draft a report that cites record ids, and a person signs.

assumptions: The note is the manager's words.
Configure the document store before a new tool.
unknowns: Whether a vendor note is a contract.
research_questions: How often a problem is resolved only after a second meeting.

already_counted.description: The meetings stay inside the remaining time of those steps.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only assembly and filing move to a job. The meeting, the decision, and the signature stay with the manager, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.short: Review project plans and coordinate the work.

steps.what: Review project plans to coordinate activity
Check plan dates against the project record

outputs: filed copy of signed coordination note v1

tasks.design: A job checks dates on the plan in {PROJECT}. The manager reviews the plan, coordinates the activity, signs the note, and a job files that version. A date clash is not resolved by the job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were reviewed from a copy that had drifted from the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan dates can be compared with a fixed rule.
tasks.still_hard: Coordination still needs the manager to move people and scope.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what moves and what waits.

ambition.what: Flag a date clash the day the plan record changes, before the note is signed.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the review on coordination, not on hunting dates.

reach.learn: Which date clash the note accepted

evidence.claim: The management digest says security and IT work uses ticket and incident-log configuration, and judgement stays manual.
The management digest says a records path can draft a report that cites record ids, and a person signs.

assumptions: Configure the project record before a new store.
unknowns: Who else must sign a date move.
research_questions: How often the plan record is behind the real work.

already_counted.description: Reviewing the plan stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

tasks.short: Assign and review the work of analysts and programmers.

steps.what: Assign and review work of programmers and analysts
List open tickets without scoring any worker
Sign the assignment of computer-related workers

outputs: filed copy of signed assignment v1

tasks.design: A dashboard lists open tickets in {HELPDESK} with no score of a person. The manager assigns and reviews the work of analysts and programmers, signs the assignment in {PROJECT}, and a job files that version. A model does not allocate the work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments were verbal, and a queue view could be turned into a ranking of people.
tasks.enabler_now: The ticket log can list open work without a score.
tasks.still_hard: Who should do the work still depends on skill and load the manager knows.
tasks.human_edge: The manager assigns the work and reviews it.
tasks.altitude: Assignment stays with the manager. Listing tickets and filing the signed list shrink.

reach.task: Do the work named in the signed assignment
reach.learn: That the list is not a score

evidence.claim: Digest [S10] bars a significant decision about a person made solely by automation, so assignment and hiring stay with the manager.
Digest [S11] treats allocation and performance scoring of people as high-risk employment uses, so this design does not score workers or assign them by a model.
Digest [S14] requires works-council consent for hiring, appraisal, staff data, or monitoring unless a collective agreement settles it, so this design does not add a watch or a score.

assumptions: No score or ranking of a person is stored.
Configure the ticket log before a new tool.
unknowns: Whether the works council must see an assignment template.
Who may view another person's assignments.
research_questions: How the manager wants load described without becoming a score.

already_counted.description: Assigning and reviewing the work stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap ticket or ledger fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only assembly and filing move to a job. The meeting, the decision, and the signature stay with the manager, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The information systems manager spends the week on priorities, people, and the signed decision. Ticket totals and filing a signed note move to a job. A backup that already runs is not saved labour.
reach: Service desk leads receive a signed priority list instead of a verbal shuffle.
Analysts see the assignment the manager signed, not a score.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report figure that has no ticket or ledger row.
Keep hiring, assignment, and access changes as their own decision.
role.ambitious_version: A signed priority list can open the week's work board, and the manager still releases it.
